S1.title: Wikipedia EN, Seville
S1.quote: The city surrendered on 23 November 1248, after fifteen months of siege. … Seville was chosen as headquarters of the Casa de Contratación in 1503, which was the decisive development for Seville becoming the port and gateway to the Indies. … The first tribunal of the Spanish Inquisition was instituted in Seville in 1478. … reduced the population by almost half … 1842 100,498 — 1857 112,529 +12.0% 1877 133,247 +18.4% 1887 143,840 +7.9% 1900 147,271 +2.4% 1910 153,258 +4.1% 1920 205,723 +34.2% 1930 217,788 +5.9% 1940 302,300 +38.8% 1950 374,138 +23.8% 1960 441,869 +18.1% 1970 545,692 +23.5% 1981 645,817 +18.3% 1991 683,028 +5.8% 2001 684,633 +0.2% 2011 698,042 +2.0% 2021 684,340 −2.0% Source: INE … Seville has a municipal population of about 688,714 as of 2025 … By the end of the 12th century, the walled enclosure perhaps contained 80,000 inhabitants. … The city's bullring , the Real Maestranza , was designed in 1761 by Vicente San Martin. … Until the economic crisis of 2007, this urban area saw significant population growth … the current building is a massive Gothic structure begun after 1401 and finished in 1506

S2.title: Wikipedia EN, History of Seville
S2.quote: On 30 May 1252, King Ferdinand III died in the Alcázar; he was buried in the cathedral, formerly the great mosque … The city was chosen for the first auto de fe , after which six people were burned alive on 6 February 1481. … On 1 February, Marshal Claude Victor occupied the city, accompanied by the pretender to the Spanish throne, Joseph Bonaparte (José I) … The French settled in until 27 August 1812, when they were forced to retreat by Anglo-Spanish counterattacks … Construction began in 1728, and proceeded intermittently for the next 30 years. … One of the first large industrial building projects in modern Europe, the Royal Tobacco Factory … In 1835–1837 the Ecclesiastical Confiscations of Mendizábal involved the national confiscation and sale of church property … On 18 July General Gonzalo Queipo de Llano quickly gained control of the 2nd División Orgánica … Seville was thus occupied by the rebels along with Cadiz and Algeciras … Francoist Spain (1939–1975) … since 1989, it has been home to the Presidency of the Andalusian Autonomous Government (Junta de Andalucía) … damaging the Giralda and killing nine people … The Second Republic and Civil War (1931–1939) … The city surrendered on 23 November 1248. … In 45 BC, after the Roman Civil War ended at the Battle of Munda , Híspalis built city walls and a forum … Carthaginians had caused the collapse of Tartessos by 530 BC … Preparations and construction began in 1910 for the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929

S3.title: Wikipedia EN, Giralda
S3.quote: The metal spheres that originally topped the tower fell during the 1356 earthquake, and the spheres were replaced in 1400 with a cross and bell. … The new belfry was constructed between 1558 and 1568. … In the 16th century Hernán Ruiz the Younger , who was commissioned to work on cathedral, constructed a new Renaissance-style belfry extension at the top of the tower … Upon returning to al-Andalus in 1184 for a new military campaign, Aby Ya'qub Yusuf ordered the construction of the minaret. … On 10 March 1198, the tower was completed … During the 1755 Lisbon earthquake it suffered damage but repairs were not performed until 1770 … It brings the height of the tower to approximately 95 or 96 meters.

S4.title: Wikipedia EN, Seville Cathedral
S4.quote: In July 1401, city leaders decided to build a new cathedral to replace the grand mosque that served as the cathedral until then. … Work began in 1402 and continued for over a century. … It is one of the largest churches in the world and the largest Gothic cathedral. … The new mosque was dedicated in 1182, but was not completed until 1198. … the current crossing lantern, with its ornate lierne vaulting , was designed by Juan Gil de Hontañón the Elder in 1513 and completed in 1519

S5.title: Wikipedia EN, Torre del Oro
S5.quote: The Tower of Gold was built 1220–1221, by order of the Almohad governor of Seville, Abu l-Ulà, with a twelve-sided base. … Rebuilding of the third level was made by Brusselian military engineer Sebastian Van der Borcht in 1760. … The tower was badly damaged by the Lisbon earthquake of 1755

S6.title: Wikipedia EN, Alcázar of Seville
S6.quote: A Latin inscription on the palace façade includes the year 1364 while an Arabic inscription in the Hall of Ambassadors gives the year 1366, which indicate the probable dates for the start and completion of construction, respectively. … Towards 1150, the Almohad Caliphate began to develop Seville as their capital in al-Andalus. … Much of the old Gothic Palace of Alfonso X was destroyed during the 1755 Lisbon earthquake .

S7.title: Wikipedia EN, Casa de Contratación
S7.quote: was established by the Crown of Castile , in 1503 in the port of Seville (and transferred to Cádiz in 1717) as a crown agency for the Spanish Empire … In 1717 they moved the Casa from Seville to Cádiz , diminishing Seville's importance in international trade.

S8.title: Wikipedia EN, Great Plague of Seville
S8.quote: The Great Plague of Seville (1647–1652) was a massive outbreak of disease in Spain that killed up to a quarter of Seville 's population.

S9.title: Wikipedia EN, Triana Bridge
S9.quote: It was built during the reign of Isabella II of Spain and completed in 1852 as the first solid bridge in Seville, replacing an earlier floating bridge consisting of boats (a pontoon bridge ). … First built by the Moors in the 12th century, the pontoon bridge managed to exist for seven centuries due to later repairs.

S10.title: Wikipedia EN, Walls of Seville
S10.quote: The walls remained intact until the 19th century, when they were partially demolished after the revolution of 1868 . … Some parts of the walls still exist, especially around the Alcázar of Seville and some curtain walls in the barrio de la Macarena . … In 1023, Abu al-Qasim first King Taifa of Seville (1023–1042), ordered the walls to be raised again to protect the city from Christian troops, and between the 11th century and 12th century a major expansion that doubled the walled enclosure took place. … The city has been surrounded by walls since the Roman period … In late 2021, for the first time, the remains of a section of the Roman wall of Seville were discovered.

S11.title: Wikipedia EN, Plaza Nueva (Seville)
S11.quote: The land which the plaza is built on was formerly part of the San Fernando convent from 1270 to 1840. … The plaza was completed in 1856. … Construction start 1852 Completed 1856

S12.title: Wikipedia EN, Alameda de Hércules
S12.quote: Before its urban transformation, the Alameda square was a fragment of the easternmost branch of the Guadalquivir River. … In 1574, the Count of Barajas further drained the water, building irrigation channels and fountains, and planting lines of waterside white poplar trees. … Built in 1574, it was originally a promenaded public garden

S13.title: Wikipedia EN, Guadalquivir
S13.quote: This was below that recorded in Seville in the flood of 1963 when 6,000 m 3 /s … During the 16th century, the silting up of the Guadalquivir became ever more serious and started to halt navigation on the river. … The construction of the canal known as the Corta de Merlina in 1794 marked the beginning of the modernisation of the port of Seville.

S14.title: Wikipedia EN, Ibero-American Exposition of 1929
S14.quote: was a world's fair held in Seville , Spain , from 9 May 1929 until 21 June 1930

S15.title: Wikipedia EN, Plaza de España (Seville)
S15.quote: It was built in 1928 for the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929 . … In 1929, Seville hosted the Ibero-American Exposition World's Fair , located in the celebrated Maria Luisa Park

S16.title: Wikipedia EN, Expo 92
S16.quote: was a universal exhibition held from Monday 20 April to Monday 12 October 1992, at the Isla de La Cartuja , in Seville , Spain. … The site of the exposition covered 215 hectares (530 acres) … Five more new bridges were built over the Guadalquivir river: Alamillo , Barqueta , Cartuja, Cristo de la Expiración, and Delicias.

S17.title: Wikipedia EN, Alamillo Bridge
S17.quote: Construction of the bridge began in 1989 and was completed in 1992 from a design by Santiago Calatrava .

S18.title: Wikipedia EN, Puente de la Barqueta
S18.quote: It was built between 1989 and 1992, on the occasion of the Universal Exposition Expo'92

S19.title: Wikipedia EN, Centenario Bridge
S19.quote: building works took place from 1989 to 1991. … The bridge opened on 15 November 1991. … with a main span of 265 metres (869 ft) and a maximum height of 102 metres (335 ft)

S20.title: Wikipedia EN, Metropol Parasol
S20.quote: was completed in April 2011, and is roughly 150 by 70 metres (490 by 230 ft) with an approximate height of 26 metres (85 ft) … Construction began on June 26, 2005 … The market itself remained until 1973, when the remainder of the dilapidated market building was finally demolished. … The land remained undeveloped until 1990

S21.title: Wikipedia EN, Torre Sevilla
S21.quote: Its construction started in March 2008 and was completed in 2015. … The tower is the tallest building in Andalusia and in the city of Seville

S22.title: Wikipedia EN, Seville-Santa Justa railway station
S22.quote: Opened 2 May 1991 … The Madrid–Seville high-speed rail line was opened in 1992

S23.title: Wikipedia EN, Isla Mágica
S23.quote: the theme park was later redesigned and it reopened as Isla Mágica on 28 June 1997.

S24.title: Wikipedia EN, Los Remedios (Seville)
S24.quote: In the 1960s a large-scale urbanization took place, and the new residential construction led to the city's first planned neighbourhood. … In 1945 the Avenida de la Republica Argentina was built

S25.title: Wikipedia EN, Ferdinand Magellan
S25.quote: In Seville , he married, fathered two children, and organized the expedition. … The fleet left Spain on 20 September 1519

S27.title: Wikipedia EN, Second Spanish Republic
S27.quote: The Republic was proclaimed on 14 April 1931 after the deposition of King Alfonso XIII .

S28.title: Wikipedia EN, Spanish transition to democracy
S28.quote: Death of Franco 20 November 1975 … Constitution adopted 29 December 1978

S29.title: Wikipedia EN, Almoravid dynasty
S29.quote: In September 1091, al-Mu'tamid surrendered Seville to the Almoravids and was exiled to Aghmat.

S30.title: Wikipedia EN, Almohad Caliphate
S30.quote: Between 1146 and 1173, the Almohads gradually wrested control from the Almoravids over the Muslim principalities in Iberia. … The Almohads transferred the capital of Muslim Iberia from Córdoba to Seville .

S32.title: Wikipedia EN, Tartessos
S32.quote: a historical civilization settled in the southern Iberian Peninsula from about the late Bronze Age until the 5th century BC

S33.title: Wikipedia EN, Seville (Hispalis, Umayyad conquest)
S33.quote: The town was called Hisbaal by the Phoenicians and by the Tartessians, the indigenous pre-Roman Iberian people of Tartessos , who controlled the Guadalquivir Valley at the time. … Following Roman rule, there were successive conquests of the Roman province of Hispania Baetica by the Germanic Vandals , Suebi and Visigoths during the 5th and 6th centuries. … Seville ( Spalis ) was seemingly taken by Musa ibn Nusayr in the late summer of 712

S35.title: Wikipedia ES, Puerto de Sevilla
S35.quote: Los trabajos de la corta de Tablada comenzaron en 1909. … Se reanudaron en 1919 y quedaron terminaron en 1926. … En 1927 elaboró el conocido como "Plan Brackenbury", que convertiría el Guadalquivir a su paso por Sevilla en una dársena cerrada al sur por una esclusa, pasando el río vivo por San Juan de Aznalfarache y la Vega de Triana. … Las obras del nuevo cauce por la Vega de Triana se suspendieron en 1933 y continuaron en 1943. … Las obras del "Plan Brackenbury" de 1927 no terminaron hasta 1951. … En 1951 se construyó la esclusa al sur del puerto.

S36.title: Wikipedia ES, Canal de Alfonso XIII
S36.quote: se creó un nuevo cauce por la Cartuja , que se unió en San Juan de Aznalfarache con el antiguo cauce abandonado tras la creación del canal de Alfonso XIII, y se taponó el río en Chapina, la entrada norte del río en Sevilla. … Con las obras de la Exposición Universal de 1992 se volvió a abrir el tapón de Chapina, desplazándose su final más hacia el norte, hasta la zona de San Jerónimo

S37.title: Wikipedia ES, Plaza de toros de la Real Maestranza
S37.quote: Entre 1761 y 1765 se construyó la portada interior y, sobre la misma, el palco del Príncipe. … La construcción de la plaza estuvo paralizada entre 1766 y 1784. … En 1876 se le encargó al arquitecto Juan Talavera de la Vega la finalización de la plaza.

S38.title: Wikipedia ES, Plaza de la Encarnación (Sevilla)
S38.quote: A principio del siglo XIX , durante la invasión francesa, se derribó el convento de la Encarnación, y se construyó en el centro un mercado de tres calles cubiertas de galerías. … En 1948 se planteó la ampliación del eje principal de Campana - Osario , por lo que se derribó el tercio meridional del mercado … lo que restaba del mercado fue demolido en 1973 debido a su estado ruinoso.

S39.title: Wikipedia ES, Puente de Isabel II (Sevilla)
S39.quote: Su construcción finalizó en 1852, bajo el reinado de Isabel II … Solo en 1845, cuando se iniciaron las obras de construcción del actual puente

S40.title: Wikipedia ES, Historia de Sevilla
S40.quote: Para la Exposición de 1929 construyeron dos plazas: la Plaza de España y la Plaza de América . … La peste negra de 1348, el gran terremoto del año 1355

zones.name: Almohad walled city (Ishbiliya)
zones.note: City full at the start year (rule r/Madrid). S1: the walled enclosure perhaps held 80,000 people by the end of the 12th century; S10: the walls were raised in 1023 and expanded in the 11th-12th centuries doubling the enclosure. Ring = legacy walls_1248.json (georeferenced from IAPH figure, approximate). Born 1225 is the legacy convention (everything standing by 1248).

walls.name: Almohad walls (Islamic circuit on the Roman line)
walls.note: S10: surrounded by walls since the Roman period; the Taifa raised them in 1023 and an 11th-12th c. expansion doubled the enclosure; partially demolished after the 1868 revolution; sections survive around the Alcázar and in the Macarena. Almohad raising 1170-1210 and demolition "1858-c.1873" come from the scheda (S55, not re-fetched). CONFLICT: S10 says after 1868, the scheda says from 1858 -> demolition window set to 1868-1873 (start from S10, end from S55). Height 10 m, width 4 m, tower spacing 45 m = modelling parameters [Guessing]. The Roman wall (Caesar; a 3rd c. section found in 2021, S10) predates the start year and no sourced ring exists: NOT modelled, the 1248 ring follows the later Islamic circuit [Likely].

water.note: Ring from data_sevilla_src/water_src.json (owner georeferencing). Owner decision 23 Oct: lake present from 1992 (Expo opens 20 April 1992, S16).

bridges.name: San Telmo Bridge
bridges.note: Year 1931 from the legacy bridges_sevilla.py ([V] in a source file that is no longer in the repo): not re-verified. S36 only confirms the bridge exists over the dársena.

bridges.name: Los Remedios Bridge
bridges.note: Year 1968 from the legacy bridges_sevilla.py, not re-verified.

bridges.name: Delicias Bridge
bridges.note: S16: built for Expo 92 (opening 1992); 1990 = owner decision 22 Oct (sources say 1990 or 1992).

bridges.name: Cachorro Bridge (Cristo de la Expiración)
bridges.note: S16: built for Expo 92; 1991 is the legacy year.

bridges.name: Cartuja Footbridge
bridges.note: S16: built for Expo 92; 1991 is the legacy owner decision.

landmarks.name: Giralda
landmarks.note: Almohad minaret ordered 1184, finished 10 March 1198 (S3); Renaissance belfry 1558-1568 by Hernán Ruiz the Younger (S3), ~95-96 m with the belfry (S3). Width 13 m and the body/belfry split are approximations [Guessing]; the 1356-1400 loss of the spheres is not modelled.

landmarks.name: Great Mosque
landmarks.note: S4: the new mosque was dedicated in 1182 and completed in 1198 (phase 1182-1198); "Christianized mosque" 1248-1401; city leaders decided to replace it in July 1401. Demolition window 1402-1434 is a modelling choice tied to the Cathedral works (S4: work began 1402). Height 16 m = legacy [Guessing].

landmarks.name: Cathedral
landmarks.note: S4: work began in 1402 and continued for over a century; the crossing lantern (designed 1513) was completed in 1519; "one of the largest churches in the world and the largest Gothic cathedral". S1: begun after 1401 and finished in 1506. Nave 38 m = [Guessing]. The legacy/scheda start 1434 (Ysambert in charge) is replaced by 1402.

landmarks.name: Torre del Oro
landmarks.note: S5: built 1220-1221 with a twelve-sided base; third level rebuilt in 1760 after the 1755 earthquake. Radius 7.5 m and height 36 m are approximations [Guessing] (legacy 38 m). The 1760 top is not modelled as a second phase.

landmarks.name: Real Alcázar
landmarks.note: S6: the Almohads developed Seville as capital from c.1150 and built the Al-Muwarak palace on the Alcázar site; the Palace of Peter dates from 1364-1366 (inscriptions, S6, not modelled as a phase). The 1150-1200 span is a modelling choice [Guessing]; no cadastre building within 30 m: params 120 x 100 m, orientation unset [Guessing].

landmarks.name: Maestranza Bullring
landmarks.note: S37: inner portal built 1761-1765; construction paralysed 1766-1784; architect commissioned in 1876 to finish it (the 19th century). S1: designed in 1761. The end 1881 is from the scheda (S60, not re-fetched). Height 16 m = legacy.

landmarks.name: Pontoon bridge
landmarks.note: S9: pontoon bridge first built by the Moors in the 12th century, lasted ~700 years until the Isabel II bridge (1852). 1171 is from the scheda (S62, not re-fetched). Axis and length approximated [Guessing]; box model.

landmarks.name: Isabel II Bridge
landmarks.note: S9: completed in 1852, first solid bridge in Seville; S39: works began in 1845 when the boat bridge was moved. Iron bridge modelled with the stone-arch preset (3 spans) [Guessing]; length/width from the OSM outline.

landmarks.name: Macarena walls
landmarks.note: S10: the Puerta de la Macarena is of Almoravid origin and curtain walls in the Macarena survive; scheda: Almoravid circuit 1120-1140, Almohad raising 1170-1210 (S55). Span = Almoravid rule of Seville 1091-1147 (S29), modelling choice; line = a stretch of the legacy 1248 ring [Guessing]. Not demolished.

landmarks.name: Plaza Nueva
landmarks.note: S11: construction started 1852, completed 1856. CONFLICT: the scheda (S59, not re-fetched) says demolition 1848, completed 1853, inaugurated 1857. Flat paving block 90 x 120 m from the legacy PLAZAS box.

landmarks.name: Plaza de España
landmarks.note: S15: "built in 1928 for the Ibero-American Exposition of 1929"; S40: built for the 1929 Exposition. The 1914 start is the scheda/BOE project year (S61, not re-fetched) -> conf low. Real plan is a semicircle: the courtyard preset (180 x 70 m, orientation unset) is an approximation [Guessing]; no cadastre building within 30 m.

landmarks.name: Los Remedios
landmarks.note: District anchor (label), not a monument: footprint = the cadastre building at the point, so the shape does not change. S24: large-scale urbanization in the 1960s, the city's first planned neighbourhood; Avenida de la República Argentina built 1945.

landmarks.name: Cartuja Island
landmarks.note: Expo 92 site anchor (label): no cadastre building within 30 m, so only a 0.15 m slab is built (no invented building). S16: 215-hectare Expo site on the Isla de La Cartuja, 20 April - 12 October 1992; works 1987-1992 per the scheda (S64, not re-fetched), 1989 start is the bridge works year (S17-S19).

landmarks.name: Barqueta Bridge
landmarks.note: S18: built 1989-1992 for Expo 92. The real bridge is a single steel arch with hangers: modelled with the arch preset, no hangers [Guessing]; axis from the OSM outline.

landmarks.name: Alamillo Bridge
landmarks.note: S17: construction began in 1989, completed 1992 (design concept 1987). The cable-stayed pylon (140 m in the legacy) cannot be made by a preset: deck only; the bespoke legacy geometry in bridges_sevilla.py remains the model of record.

landmarks.name: Centenario Bridge
landmarks.note: S19: works 1989-1991, opened 15 November 1991 (1991.87); 565 m long, main span 265 m, maximum height 102 m. Deck only with the arch preset; pylon/cables not modelled (see bridges_sevilla.py).

landmarks.name: Metropol Parasol
landmarks.note: S20: construction began 26 June 2005, completed April 2011, about 150 x 70 m, ~26 m high (legacy 32 m). Pergola preset approximates the waffle canopy.

landmarks.name: Torre Sevilla
landmarks.note: S21: construction started March 2008, completed 2015, 180.5 m, tallest building in Andalusia.

landmarks.name: Santa Justa station
landmarks.note: S22: opened 2 May 1991. The 1989 start is the legacy/scheda year (visitasevilla page, not re-fetched). The cadastre parcel (418 x 149 m) is too large for the preset: footprint ignored (max_fp 120), params 110 x 120 m used.

landmarks.name: Isla Mágica
landmarks.note: Theme-park anchor (label): no cadastre building within 30 m, so only a 0.15 m slab is built (no invented building). S23: reopened as Isla Mágica on 28 June 1997 (it was first a different park); no construction start in the fetched text.

landmarks.name: Encarnación
landmarks.note: S38: a three-aisle market was built in the middle of the square during the French invasion; 1820 = scheda (S52, not re-fetched). Southern third demolished 1948, rest in 1973 (S38, S20). The 1973 end is modelled; box size from the legacy lost-building code.

soste.caption: The Great Mosque gives way to the Cathedral (1401)
The Casa de Contratación opens the Americas trade (1503)
The Giralda gets its Renaissance belfry (1558-1568)
Isabel II Bridge replaces the boat bridge (1845-1852)
Plaza de España for the 1929 Expo (1914-1929)
The river is moved west: Corta de la Cartuja (1975-1982)

title: SEVILLE
1248 TO NOW

cards.title: Ferdinand III takes Seville
lines: After fifteen months of siege, the Almohad city surrenders to Castile.

cards.title: The king dies in Seville
lines: Ferdinand III dies in the Alcázar and is buried in the old mosque, now the cathedral.

cards.title: A city of about 50,000
lines: A rough estimate puts the walled city at about 50,000 people.
cards.note: Scheda D estimate, source not re-fetched; S1 says perhaps 80,000 by the end of the 12th century.

cards.title: Earthquake
lines: The Giralda's metal spheres fall.
cards.note: S40 (Spanish Wikipedia) dates the great earthquake 1355; S3 says 1356.

cards.title: Peter's palace
lines: Inscriptions date the palace of Peter in the Alcázar to 1364-1366.
cards.note: S6 calls them the probable start and completion dates.

cards.title: A Christian crown
lines: A cross and a bell replace the spheres on the Giralda.

cards.title: Cathedral works begin
lines: In 1401 city leaders decide to replace the great mosque; work starts in 1402.

cards.title: The Inquisition begins here
lines: The first tribunal of the Spanish Inquisition is set up in Seville; the first auto de fe follows in 1481.

cards.title: Gateway to the Americas
lines: The Casa de Contratación makes Seville the port of the Indies.

cards.title: Magellan sets out
lines: Organized in Seville, the fleet leaves Spain on 20 September 1519.

cards.title: A new top for the Giralda
lines: Hernán Ruiz the Younger builds the Renaissance belfry, 1558-1568.

cards.title: The lagoon is drained
lines: An old river branch becomes the Alameda de Hércules.

cards.title: Golden Age Seville
lines: Estimates put the city near 120,000 people.
cards.note: Scheda D estimate, not re-fetched.

cards.title: The Great Plague
lines: Estimates of the dead range from a quarter to almost half of the city.
cards.note: S8: up to a quarter; S1: almost half. No reliable count.

cards.title: A shrinking city
lines: The population is estimated at about 70,000.
cards.note: S1: the plague cut the population by almost half and it did not recover until the early 19th century.

cards.title: Trade moves to Cádiz
lines: The Casa de Contratación leaves Seville.

cards.title: Royal Tobacco Factory
lines: Work starts on one of the first large industrial buildings in modern Europe.

cards.title: Lisbon earthquake
lines: The Giralda and the Torre del Oro are damaged; nine people die in Seville.
cards.note: Date 1 November 1755 is general knowledge, not in the fetched texts: the year is sourced.

cards.title: Torre del Oro
lines: Its third level is rebuilt after the earthquake.

cards.title: French occupation
lines: Marshal Victor occupies the city on 1 February 1810.

cards.title: Encarnación convent demolished
lines: The convent comes down during the French occupation.
cards.note: Year 1811 from the scheda (S52, not re-fetched); S38 says early 19th century, during the French invasion.

cards.title: A market square
lines: A market with three covered aisles rises on the Encarnación site.
cards.note: Year 1820 from the scheda (S52, not re-fetched); S38 gives no year.

cards.title: Church property is sold off
lines: The Mendizábal confiscations of 1835-1837 put church property up for sale.

cards.title: 100,498 people
lines: The municipal census counts 100,498 residents.

cards.title: Isabel II Bridge opens
lines: The first solid bridge in Seville replaces a pontoon bridge that lasted almost seven centuries.
cards.note: Exact day (23 Feb 1852 in the legacy) not in the fetched texts: the year is sourced.

cards.title: Plaza Nueva
lines: A convent site becomes a square, begun in 1852 and finished in 1856.
cards.note: Scheda says demolition 1848, inauguration 1857 (S59, not re-fetched).

cards.title: 112,529 people
lines: The city has grown by 12% since 1842.

cards.title: The walls come down
lines: After the 1868 revolution the walls are partly demolished; the Macarena stretch survives.
cards.note: Scheda: demolition 1858-c.1873 (S55, not re-fetched).

cards.title: Finishing the Maestranza
lines: An architect is hired to complete the bullring, unfinished since the 1760s.

cards.title: 133,247 people
lines: Census figure.

cards.title: 147,271 people
lines: The city is still mostly inside its old circuit.
cards.note: The second line is an interpretation of the density data, not a quoted claim [Likely].

cards.title: Alfonso XIII Canal
lines: Work starts on the Tablada cut; it resumes in 1919 and ends in 1926.

cards.title: The Guadalquivir floods
lines: The river floods in February 1917.
cards.note: Scheda F only, not re-fetched.

cards.title: The river will move
lines: A plan turns the old river into a dock and sends the river west of Triana.
cards.note: S35 Plan Brackenbury 1927; works finished in 1951.

cards.title: Ibero-American Exposition
lines: Plaza de España and María Luisa Park open to the world.

cards.title: Spanish Civil War
lines: On 18 July General Queipo de Llano takes Seville for the rebels.

cards.title: 302,300 people
lines: Census figure.

cards.title: Chapina is plugged
lines: The old river entrance is closed; the city side becomes a dock.
cards.note: Years 1948-1950 from the scheda (S51, not re-fetched); S36 confirms the plug.

cards.title: Los Remedios
lines: A large planned neighbourhood rises on the west bank.

cards.title: Tamarguillo flood
lines: The Tamarguillo overflows and floods much of the city.
cards.note: Scheda only (25 November 1961), not re-fetched.

cards.title: Another flood
lines: The Guadalquivir peaks at 6,000 cubic meters per second, the record in Seville.
cards.note: S13 gives the year 1963 and the flow; March is from the scheda (S54).

cards.title: 545,692 people
lines: Census figure.

cards.title: Encarnación market demolished
lines: The square stays empty for decades, used as parking.

cards.title: Corta de la Cartuja
lines: A new river channel west of La Cartuja is cut against floods.
cards.note: Years 1975-1982 from the scheda (S56, S57, not re-fetched); S36 confirms the cut and the Chapina plug.

cards.title: Spain turns to democracy
lines: Franco dies on 20 November 1975; the Constitution follows in 1978.

cards.title: 645,817 people
lines: Census figure.

cards.title: Expo bridges rise
lines: Work starts on the Alamillo, Barqueta and Centenario bridges.

cards.title: Andalusian government
lines: The presidency of the Junta de Andalucía settles at San Telmo.
cards.note: S2 says since 1989; the month is a placeholder.

cards.title: The plug moves north
lines: For Expo 92 the Chapina plug is reopened and moved to San Jerónimo.
cards.note: S36 gives no year ("with the Expo works"): 1990 is a placeholder inside the works period.

cards.title: Santa Justa station
lines: The new railway station opens on 2 May 1991.

cards.title: Centenario Bridge
lines: A 565 m cable-stayed bridge opens on 15 November 1991.

cards.title: Expo 92 opens
lines: 20 April - 12 October 1992, on La Cartuja.

cards.title: High-speed rail
lines: The Madrid-Seville high-speed line opens in 1992.

cards.title: Isla Mágica
lines: A theme park opens on the old Expo grounds on 28 June 1997.

cards.title: 684,633 people
lines: The city holds steady while the metro area keeps growing until 2007.

cards.title: Metropol Parasol
lines: "Las Setas", a giant wooden canopy, is completed over the Encarnación square.

cards.title: Torre Sevilla
lines: At 180.5 m it becomes Andalusia's tallest building.

cards.title: Seville today
lines: 688,714 people.
